FY2020 Financial Statements Finance & Facilities Committee October 23, 2020 9:00 am

Financial Statements for Fiscal 2020 •Audited by O’Connor & Drew, external auditors •State Auditor has reviewed and approved them subject to Board of Trustees approval •Finance and Facilities Committee reviews today for recommendation to the full Board for approval tomorrow

The financial statements and the budget are presented differently • The financial statements follow Government Accounting Standards Board (GASB) accounting rules, which incorporate accrual accounting principles • Include depreciation • Match revenues and expenses • Show interest but not the current principal portion of long term debt as an expense • Classify capital maintenance expenses as increases to capital assets, not an expense • Include the URI Foundation and Alumni Engagement and the URI Research Foundation as “component units” • Include estimates of State ERS pension and OPEB liabilities that are actuarially adjusted each year and allocated to the agencies • Reflect many eliminating entries for transfers between funds (e.g. Foundation to the University)

The financial statements and the budget are presented differently •The budget is based on cash accounting and divides the budget into Education & General (“unrestricted”) funds and Auxiliary, Sponsored Research and other (“restricted”) funds • Shows debt service on GO Bonds as “revenue” from the state, then shows a matching entry as an expense; the debt service is the obligation of the State • Revenues include the annual appropriation for the State Crime Lab • Federal loans and external scholarships included as revenue and expense - GASB treats as a pass-through • Operating expenses include maintenance items that are considered capital expenditures under GASB • Principal portion of debt service included as an expense • Auxiliary enterprises budget expenses to match anticipated revenue

Financial statements are important to the financial markets URI has two main types of debt obligations: •Revenue bonds – issued through RIHEBC and secured by a pledge of our Education and General (E&G) revenues or our Auxiliary (Aux) revenues - $292 mm •Certificates of Participation (COPS) – issued by the State, serviced by payments made by agencies (such as URI) to the State - $22 mm General Obligation (GO) bonds are obligations of the State of Rhode Island, not the University, and the State pays the debt service on them

The agencies that rate our bonds analyze our financial statements •GASB standardization permits comparisons among many financial institutions •Moody’s and Standard & Poor use financial statements as the basis of their ratings analysis •Our revenue bonds have a debt service coverage ratio requirement: •E&G DSC requirement is 1.0 times •Aux DSC requirement is 1.2 times •Failure to achieve these ratios is not an event of default •But it does prevent us from issuing additional revenue bonds until the ratio is achieved again

The budget is the financial management tool used by the University and the State •Reflects the State’s approach to determining the annual State appropriation for the University •Reflects the fact that E&G funds may not be used to support activities that are required to be self-supporting (auxiliaries, research, etc) •Reflects cash accounting rather than accrual accounting

MEMORANDUM To: David M. Dooley, Ph.D. President, University of Rhode Island From: Donald H. DeHayes Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs Date: October 2, 2020 Subj: Approval of Tenure and Rank of Professor for Dr. Gaurav Khanna I am pleased to recommend approval of tenured status at the rank of Professor of Physics Sciences for Dr. Gaurav Khanna. The dean of the College of Arts and Sciences, Dr. Jeannette Riley, has evaluated Dr. Khanna’s credentials - he was previously a faculty member in the Department of Physics at UMass Dartmouth and will be joining URI as Director of Research Computing in ITS. As the chief academic officer, I have reviewed Dr. Khanna’s record, as well as the recommendations of the dean and our CIO, Karlis Kaugars, and I concur in the recommendation that he be awarded tenure at the rank of Professor in the College of Arts and Sciences. I now ask you to seek the Board of Trustees’ endorsement of the recommendation for the granting of tenure and rank of Professor to Dr. Gaurav Khanna. Thank you. c: M. DeHayes, Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs 110 Green Hall Kingston, RI. 02881 VIA EMAIL AND CAMPUS MAIL Dear Provost DeHayes: I write this letter in support of tenure in the Department of Physics, College of Arts & Sciences, for Dr.
Gaurav Khanna.
As you know, Dr.
Khanna will be joining URI as Director of Research Computing.
He is currently a full professor of physics at the University of Massachusetts-Dartmouth.
The offer of a tenured professorship in URI’s Department of Physics, contingent upon Board approval, was made part of URI’s offer of employment to Dr.
Khanna.
This matter was taken up by the Department of Physics this summer, which supported Dr.
Khanna’s tenure by a vote of 7-0 with one abstention.
As you can see from his curriculum vitae, Dr.
Khanna has an excellent research record.
He has published in many prestigious scientific journals and presented his research at leading conferences in his field.

In all, he has over eighty-five (85) publications in peer-reviewed journals and conference proceedings.
He also has an excellent record of research funding with more than ten (10) National Science Foundation grants to his credit as well as numerous grants from other federal agencies, private foundations, and industry.
Dr.
Khanna has also distinguished himself as a teacher.
He has taught a wide variety of undergraduate and graduate physics courses and has developed new courses on the topics of relativity and black holes.
He has received several awards for his teaching effectiveness.
On a personal note, I knew Dr.
Khanna during my time at UMass-Dartmouth and found him to be a valuable colleague and good citizen of the university.
In conclusion, I support the award of tenure for Dr.
Gaurav Khanna without reservation.
Sincerely, Jeannette Riley, Dean College of Arts & Sciences
